dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses ORCA-specific COPY books and subprogram calling conventions.

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (claims) processing system - daily statistics/batch job management and client-save file handling screen
purpose.summary: ORCGL99 is a screen/batch coordination program in the JMA ORCA medical receipt system. It manages daily statistical processing job status display (checking job manager DB for running/completed jobs), handles client-save file entry, and provides a status confirmation screen (L99 window) showing processing results. It acts as a result/status display subprogram invoked via MCP LINK mechanism.

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY books (32 COPY statements) for screen layouts and data areas
MCP (Message Control Program) event-driven screen navigation pattern
CALL to external subprograms: ORCSJOB, orcfiledel
EVALUATE on MCP-STATUS/MCP-EVENT for screen event handling
Japanese comments encoded in Latin-1 (actually EUC-JP or Shift-JIS)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS - uses proprietary ORCA DB access layer
verdict.notes: Japanese comments are garbled due to Latin-1 decoding of what is likely EUC-JP or Shift-JIS encoding. Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of 25659 bytes. The program is clearly part of the well-known JMA ORCA open-source medical receipt system. Fixed format with a few lines slightly over 72 chars (5 long lines noted).
